item.content:encoded:
SCP-5179 is a interdimensional anomaly located in ██████. The project can only be seen on the night of the new moon. Due to it's anomalous properties, anyone enter SCP-5179 will turn into SCP-5179-1 and the process is irreversible.

Deleted at -17 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

EthanolC2H5OH

+ show block
– hide block

It's a cool idea albeit executed poorly, there is a lot of typos and grammar errors that need to be addressed and the weird white boxes make the page cluttered and difficult to read as you're constantly switching between the two parts of the article. The whole 'Youth passes as a fleeting river, star lies in the silver flower.' is quite a good addition and the fact it addresses the reader is a brilliant touch. Overall, a good concept executed and worded poorly.

JakdragonX

+ show block
– hide block

I wanted to love this, so, so badly. In truth, I really like this concept, and the disjointed aspect of the white boxes sort of peering into… "someone's (???)" inner life in this town of Astra was fun, albeit a bit off-toned.

However, unfortunately, there's just a massive level of "clutter" that can't be ignored (not even when it comes to the formatting.) The ending is also a bit… flat? Like, I can sort of see what you're attempting with it, but frankly the characters are somewhat baseless that its hard to keep track. It kind of reads like a "trying-to-remember" dream sequence, which may be intentional, but for myself personally it's hard to associate.

I really want to love this, and I see some potential. I'd love to see this rewritten and reworked, since it's just conceptually pleasing for me personally.

EDIT: Should also mention that I like the fourth-wall break (I'm always a sucker for them), but after re-reading, this time it feels entirely off-base from everything else, not to mention gimmicky at best.

SCP-5311 is an unidentified, partially-sentient “creature” that remains in constant confinement to the interiors of lengths of pipe—almost exclusively the plumbing of residential housing (pre-containment). It’s suspected to have remained dormant in the pipes of an unknown location until its accidental discovery, estimated to have been in ██ of the year 20█.

Deleted at -13 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

Scorpion451

+ show block
– hide block

The core idea here is definitely viable. Classic vanilla killer monsters are hard to pull off, but the anomaly is a good one to carry something like that. Ditch the targeting of people who know about it and the sound-trigger thing; this thing only needs the one party trick. It's a solid one.

I'm just going to do a rough breakdown here, if you take this to the forums for an overhaul and second try (and you should) PM me and I'll do a more in-depth one. I'm being a little blunt here because I think this is a strong idea but it will only work with a total overhaul.

The surface problems are tone breaks and bad formatting - scare italics in the Containment procedures, overdramatic statements of how dangerous it is, directly addressing the reader, hard-to-read paragraph organization… lots of little things that draft critique can help you address.

More than that though, you're totally missing the mark on what makes this thing a good monster, and how to present it. There's a lot here telling us we should be afraid of this thing, and not nearly enough showing us any of it. Tied into that, you also show your cards way, way too early, especially with regard to the strongest parts of this.

For instance, Don't beat us over the head with everything that qualifies as a pipe immediately in the containment procedures. Keep it subtle, just say it has to be kept x meters from tube-like structures or objects, and describe how it moves between pipes and manipulates the flow of things through them. And then let it click into place when the containment team points a gun at it. You can do the same with containment breaches demonstrating the endless series of things which can be considered tubes. There's potential for this thing to be scary as hell, it just needs to be used right.

Fragmented Memory 1289

Hmm. This place looks cozy.

Hey! Who are you? This is a restricted server.

Oh, a new friend! Hi! I'm Cubie. I am new around these parts. What's your name?

Feedback ported:

[+] from Quicksilvers
– hide block

+1 from me, simple and strange! Just a few things could be fixed up, though!

(he shifts nervously in his seat)

Usually when subjects do an action during an interview/recorded file, its italicized and is its own line. Here's an example from 4018:

PoI-4018-0: I know how easy it is to pretend that the old pretenses and euphemisms still hold up, and that people take the easy route when confronting things head on is hard. So I'm sorry for making things that much harder to cope with. But really, you know I had to do it to them.

PoI-4018-0 tosses a lit lighter onto the ground, igniting the gasoline. The fire spreads towards the recruitment center; shortly after it reaches the interior, the building goes up in flames.

PoI-4018-0: If I'm pissing you off, or…

Also, the other thing is this sentence:

The subject will be instantly transported to an alternate world which varies between subjects, however it is always a child's birthday party and a ██████████ chocolate cake is always being served.

"…it is always a child's birthday party" doesn't really fit the rest of the sentence (weird syntax) and maybe should be rewritten or reworded. The dialogue in the interview also seems a little stiff.

Sorry if I dumped a little too much crit - I just like the idea and it needs a little tweaking for it to shine more!

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-5459 is to be kept in a 5x5 meter box at all times. No one is to enter the box unless a controlled testing is taking place. 2 armed guards are to be stationed around the box and containment area, rotating every 20 hours. Anyone who is tested, or has been within 20m of SCP-5459 has to undergo a psych brief and debrief, and a day quarantine. SCP-5459 is able to enter others' minds and cause intense emotional distress if in an enraged state. SCP-5459 is agitated and enraged if more than 3 people are in his box. He will stay in normal form if calm, and if enraged may attempt to telepathically confuse others to get himself out or to harm others. Anyone who's mind has been entered by SCP-5459 are to be quarantined for seven (7) days.1 In the event of a containment breach, all personnel are advised to not approach within 20m of SCP-5459 to avoid getting controlled or enraging SCP-5459. If SCP-5459 is needed to be approached, a *maximum* of 2 personnel may approach. Any Class-D attempting to approach SCP-5459 in a containment breach must be terminated.

SCP-5138 was found in a barn in 1979. A farmer looked melted and in 1 pen was SCP-5138. SCP-5138 appears to be a chicken and turkey combined that leaves behind radioactive waste that is similar to the acidity of hydrochloric acid. This radioactive waste is known as SCP-5138-2. SCP-5138-1 instances are eggs laid by SCP-5138. They will taste like anything the consumer is craving and then will fill the consumer with joy. 10 minutes after eating SCP-5138-1 will start to melt you from the inside out. Any living thing breathing SCP-5138-2 will go unconscious and when woken up will instantly go mad. Once 2 minutes pass, the victim will see hallucinations. After 10 minutes, the victim will start wandering around acting like different barn animals. Then finally after 12 minutes the victim will scream in pain then fall to the ground. SCP-5138-1 when hatched immediately grows and becomes an adult. Studies on how this happens are still going on.

SCP-5667 is an autonomous, whole grain loaf of bread. Upon being damaged, SCP-5667 will regenerate damaged parts using contacting materials. When in contact with solid materials, a grey doughy substance will grow upon SCP-5667 filling and repairing any damaged areas of SCP-5667. This doughy substance will then harden and take on a more bread-like structure. Further analysis of the growth will reveal it to have the same chemical makeup as whatever material SCP-5667 was in physical contact with during the regeneration process. This process has been referred to as “the solid repairment effect” and can take from 30 minutes to 5 hours depending on the solidity of the materials used.

/scp-5965 (no title) by CyberKat233 deleted at -25 and three votes.

SCP 5965 is an Apple-II computer that appears brand new even tho it was discovered [REDACTED]

Feedback ported:

[+] from Nipixel_Paxel
– hide block

I see some SPaG (Spelling and Grammar) errors in the article, but I also see formatting errors.
Generally, authors will follow the guide that is linked here. You can also find this article by going onto the sidebar and clicking “How to Write an SCP.”
Anyway onto the criticism of the article itself.
The concept is interesting, however the article is a bit short and there’s no meat to it, if you get what I’m saying. Maybe flesh it out a bit, add something you find interesting about the SCP.

/scp-5188 (no title) by Duccy boi deleted at -26 and three votes.

SCP-5188 is a standard amazon box, with no anomalous effects. SCP-5188's anomalous affects only trigger when touched. When touched, SCP-5188 will suddenly sprout human arms and legs, through the bottom. It looks like a mother████ing cardboard spider. SCP-5188 will then undergo a rage state, where it will kill everything in its path by [DATA EXPUNGED] them.

Feedback ported:

[+] from DrKinyonori
– hide block

First off, I am new to this site, but I still want to give you critique.

Object Class: KETER OH GOSH RUN

Keter means hard to contain, not dangerous. Also, you should not be putting this type of emotion in your writing. Have you ever written an informative essay? Would you put 'THE CHEETAH CAN RUN SUPER FAST DANGER!' in your writing? The answer is no, and it's even more emphasized on this site.

SCP-5188's cell door must be chained by 10 heavy padlocks, have a 5 digit access code, a level 4 card reader, and voice and oral recognition. NOBODY is allowed into SCP-5188's cage UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES (See incident 5188-A-1).

This contradicts itself. You say nobody is allowed in, but it has a level 4 card reader, and an access code. If the former is the current containment procedure, you should strike-through the other part to show it's not valid anymore.

It looks like a mother████ing cardboard spider.

You're writing a research paper, and you decided to put a swear word in your formal report. You need to use plain and professional tone; this is supposed to be a research document on a dangerous object, and you need to write the part.

SCP-5188 is a standard amazon box, with no anomalous effects. SCP-5188's anomalous affects only trigger when touched. When touched, SCP-5188 will suddenly sprout human arms and legs, through the bottom.

There's no narrative to this, and it seems like 'a thing that does a dangerous thing when x happens' cliché. Is there any research into why it does this or how it magically conjures up legs and arms?

SCP-5188 will then undergo a rage state, where it will kill everything in its path by [DATA EXPUNGED] them.

But.. why? I read this and came out feeling bored, because there's no plot or anything; just a dangerous thing which does not have any form of development.

Exactly 69 seconds (1 minute and 9 seconds) after a human is killed, more "cardboard spiders" drag them away.

Wait, how are more cardboard spiders coming out? I thought there was one box which sprouted legs and arms. Also, 69? Really?

therefore they are dubbed SCP-5188-1, and are to be treated as such.

The word choice here is suboptimal. You should say something such as, '(these entities are hereinafter referred to as SCP-5188-1.)'

INCIDENT-5188-A-1:

First off, before the incident, there was a Level 4 padlock. Level 4 clearance is rarely given out to administrative personnel, and even so, why would a Level 4 administrative personnel be in close proximity to a dangerous anomaly?

Dr. ███: THE ████? Is this normal? Ill write this down.

This is not normal human dialogue. A professional researcher wouldn't say this out loud.

Dr. ███: OH ████ ITS WEARING HIS FACE AND ITS ████ING SMILING AT ME! ITS ████ING SMILING! WHAT THE F-

I thought that he would've been prepared for the inevitable, since this was already written in the document before the test (I presume.)

SCP-5188 jumps through the glass and tackles Dr. ███. It then proceeds to
[DATA EXPUNGED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

Huh? Why are there 3 redactions on 3 different lines? This makes no sense. Redactions =/= mystery value; only if they're done right. There's a good guide to redactions here.

Overall, this is a messy and rushed article, and I'm pretty sure this is a cold post as well. -1.

/a-closer-examination-of-scp-173 (A Closer Examination of SCP-173) by Kothardarastrix deleted at -15 and three votes.

Of all the anomalous objects in Foundation custody, there is one that everyone knows. We all read its file when we were in training, and for those of us who trained at Site-19, it was our first up-close and personal encounter with the anomalous. I still remember the first time I saw it; the eye-watering stink of its containment chamber, the blank stare of its fading, sprayed-on face, and, most of all, the sudden understanding that the slightest mistake would send that statue hurtling across the room to wrap its concrete hands around my neck.

Feedback ported:

[+] from Ethagon
– hide block

I like the idea of both the paper itself, the use of cross-testing for actual research, and the "conclusion" it arrives at, but there are a few things that made me downvote:

  • the size of the letters (this is the least important one)
  • Analyzing the documentation of SCP-173. This only makes sense out-of-universe. In-universe it would make more sense to frame this as an analysis of SCP-173's properties itself.
  • I think the writing could still be written a bit more clinical. It also didn't flow very well.
  • The paper makes a hypothesis at multiple points and then proceeds as if the hypothesis was proven fact. It would help a lot if more experimentation was done to support the hypothesis before moving on.
  • It would be better if the two theories at the end, quantum state and extradimensional control, were more aligned with each other. If they were more connected, it would feel more like "everything adds up" instead of a retroactive explanation for SCP-173. The quantum state theory adds a lot to these, as it really "fits" SCP-173 in a way. The extradimensional control theory, not so much.
[+] from The Pighead
– hide block

OK, so for this one, here's short reasons for why I've downvoted.

First of all, I want to be clear that I don't think your article is bad by any means. You've clearly done work about that, the grammar is perfect and the way you write it is pretty good, I've not really seem something that looked non-clinical or something like that.

But there's two reasons of why I downvote. The first one is the fact that, when I've readed some paragraphs, I've thought at least two times "Wait a minute, that looks like a SCPDeclassified post who weirdly tries to take an in-universe approach" and it felt off-topic at times (Wizz talked about the fact that in the article, 173 is a famous thing and it feels weird).

And the second reason is that, even if it's clear that you've done work and research, the paragraphs and the way it's organized looks like big walls of text, to the point that I had struggle reading that because there was too much words and too much scientific things implied, I was a bit lost.

So, that's why I downvote. But I can see a great lot of potential on your Tale, so I highly suggest you to rework it and pay attention to what others suggested you to do.

[+] from Nagiros
– hide block

Frankly I'm unconvinced that we need more 173 content in 2020. I respect the article a fair bit but I'm hardly invested in the character enough for anything resembling this.

Feedback Ported:

Unihedron

+ show block
– hide block

I'm sorry to say, but this feels really incomplete. Whatever intrigue that the article brings me remains unanswered throughout to the end and quite honestly this feels like it's written by someone who doesn't understand or bothered attempting to elaborate on why being able to hack into outright anything is anomalous, or even interesting. The name drop to UIU had a reverse impact on me; instead of making me feel "wow, they could do that?" it made me go "there's no way this makes sense".

I think this suffers a case of show-don't-tell in that I'm being told how outrageous the situation is but nothing that pulls its weight and make it feel grand, rather that it's odd being delivered this way. I think the places in the article like the breach and the high cooperation level as shown could be translated into logs that are interesting to read and experience, but in its current form it really feels lacking.

In order for an article to work, there needs to be a strong narrative with a clear beginning, middle, and end. This has a beginning and a middle. There are no stakes, just a dude who is really good at something, and has no further character development other than that. It's boring and tasteless.

/scp-5492 (no title) by CocoaIzBlu deleted at -20 and three votes.

SCP-5492 is a speaker-like object produced somewhere in the 1800s, probably tracing back to 1877. Object#: 5492 is a half-rotten spruce cuboid, plated with metal speakers made with aluminium. Its main colour is white due to the clear lack of pigmentation in SCP-5492's shape, making the wood hard to classify to the eye.

Feedback ported:

[+] from DoctorSasbo
– hide block

It's really unfortunate that everybody is downvoting this without actually commenting suggestions to help it. Here's my two cents:

The biggest issue with this imo is the prose:

  • "immensely scant amount of room, and heaps of soundproof foam" is not clinical enough for an official document. Try saying "an enclosed space insulated by soundproof foam", or state the measurements if you want to drive home the extent of it
  • "due to the lack of knowledge on SCP-5492" - If it's being researched, we already know there's a lack of knowledge, so the phrase is redundant
  • "somewhere in the 1800s, probably tracing back to 1877" - Firstly, I think you meant "sometime" instead of "somewhere." Secondly, if you have that specific of a year, it doesn't make sense to add uncertainty by saying "probably." Finally, you might want to briefly say where it's from/was found.
  • "Its main colour is white due to the clear lack of pigmentation in SCP-5492's shape, making the wood hard to classify to the eye" could just be "It is predominantly white." You're spending a lot of words elaborating on something that could be written more concisely.
  • "at the first glances… teeth to commit suicide." is too long of a sentence, try breaking it up into multiple sentences so the reader can more effectively process it
  • ""the noise is so dreadful it's better to die than live to remember the horror" - Which was said by a test subject." I get what you're going for, but it comes off as kinda flat and cliche. You might want to flesh it out a bit more with an interview log, so you can go more in detail about the effects on the subject.
  • "the unfathomable entity" doesn't fit the clinical tone. It's SCP-5492.
  • "When the surviving Subject made it out of the containment he was insane and instead of being suicidal he was critically homicidal instead." Instead of just saying he's homicidal, try describing what he did i.e. stab researchers, torture fellow D-class, etc.

Overall, I think this is a workable concept, but the execution is severely lacking. Tighten up your prose, and try to elaborate more on what actually happens so you can show instead of just telling. Hope this helps!

All Staff-enacted Deletions are carried out according to the Deletions Guide.

Summary deletions result for:

  • Articles with malicious intent
  • Pages that are clearly unfinished.
  • Attempts to "game" site procedure, such as re-posting a non-rewritten article in an attempt to get around downvotes.
  • Blatantly plagiarized material.
  • An article posted outside of the current range.

If an author attempts to self-delete their work and fails to do so properly, including either by blanking the page or renaming it, it will be deleted properly by Staff.
